vmg.label: Vision
vmg.text: A literate, self-reliant and productive community that is capable of solving its economic, social and environmental problems.

vmg.label: Mission
vmg.text: To facilitate, foster and influence a process of ongoing change in favour of the poor through community-based development.

vmg.label: Overall goal
vmg.text: To empower communities to manage their own economic, social, environmental and health problems — relying on their own skills, knowledge and resources, with minimum dependence on external support.

home.progP: A child who can read, a hillside that holds its soil, a hive that earns, a healthy mother and a village at peace are parts of the same life. EFDA works on them together, through the community’s own institutions.

programs.title: Environmental sustainability
programs.text: Communities terrace degraded hillsides, protect farmland and forest, and build fuel-saving stoves from locally available clay — easing the pressure on the trees that remain.
programs.statLabel: of degraded land rehabilitated, and over 5,000 ha of farmland protected

programs.title: Community livelihood development
programs.text: Improved beekeeping, apple orchards, youth cooperatives in small-scale animal fattening, and enset processing that opens markets to women — income that sustains a family without clearing more forest.
programs.statLabel: households in improved beekeeping, and 465 farmers now growing apples

programs.text: We work in conformity with community traditions — through elders, women and local government — from reproductive health promotion to community bylaws that end harmful practices.

home.storyP: In 2000, EFDA’s first Alternative Basic Education classes met outdoors, under trees. Since then, communities, government and EFDA have built and equipped classrooms, libraries and furniture — and education has become the thread running through every other project we run.

about.whoH2: Education as an instrument of change — in everything we do.

whoParas.text: Education For Development Association (EFDA) is an Ethiopian civil society organization working through community-based development in Oromia and Benishangul Gumuz.

Alongside standalone basic education projects run since our founding, EFDA uses education as an instrument of change in every other program — environmental protection, livelihoods, community health and peacebuilding — so that knowledge stays in the community long after a project ends.
Our education work spans Alternative Basic Education, quality improvement inside government primary schools, and the Speed School programme for children out of school for socioeconomic reasons.
